name: Wildcat Hollow Dispersed Primitive Camping - Wayne National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Athens Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for dispersed primitive camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general national forest lands outside developed fee areas. Campsites set back 100ft from trails and streams.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in rich forest topsoil, at least 200 feet from streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only within forest.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Ohio DNR / USFS fire alerts during dry spring/autumn.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state route changing to unpaved gravel forest road (Township Road 14 / Wildcat Hollow Access)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel forest roads with small washboards and dips.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (easily accessible year-round)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low to Moderate (Rolling Appalachian foothill hollows)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, blooming trillium and wildflowers, spring rainstorms, muddy trails.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (80-88°F), dense hardwood leaf canopy, high insect activity.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular Midwest autumn foliage (55-70°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), dry roads.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 30-45°F, freezing nights, light snow dustings.

dangers_and_hazards: Ticks and chiggers in brush during warm months
human_demographics_and_culture: Backcountry backpackers, Ohio University outdoor enthusiasts, digital nomads, and local hunters.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Adena and Hopewell indigenous earthwork cultures revered the hills and valleys of southeastern Ohio as sacred ancestral mound and spirit lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Calming hardwood forest grounding energy, peaceful Appalachian foothill atmosphere.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding backpacking loop through pine plantations, hardwood hollows, and rock outcrops

public_reviews_summary: Top choice for free primitive camping in Ohio. Clean forest sites, quiet surroundings, and dependable 4G/5G cell internet.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Abundant firewood.
